# The AAS volumes of 1932–1957 (AAS 24–49): the phase-2b-ii-a report

Generated by `npx tsx tools/acta-volumes-report.ts 1932-1957` from `data/documents/*.json` and `tools/fixtures/acta/` on 2026-09-13 —
the report of phase 2b-ii-a of [#25](https://github.com/CatholicOS/cmddr/issues/25) as the
[acta volumes spec](../specs/2026-09-13-acta-volumes-design.md) §6 and §9 define it: the twenty-six whole-volume OCR PDFs
of 1932–1957 -- Pius XI to his death (10 February 1939) and Pius XII from his election (2 March 1939; AAS 31 carries both),
the clean era the addendum orders first -- their chronological-index pages extracted by `tools/fetch-acta.sh` in pypdf's
layout mode (`tools/fixtures/acta/README.md` records page ranges, modes and retrieval). Each is parsed
(`tools/src/acta/index.ts`, generalised across the century's typography and OCR), classified (`categories.ts`), its pope
headings mapped (`popes.ts`), and matched to the shelf records of Pius X → Benedict XVI by issuer, date and incipit
(`match.ts`); what did not match, in a category the registry creates from the *Acta* for that pope, became a document
(`create.ts`, the phase-2a rule and guard unchanged), and everything else is listed here with its reason. The join and the
creator run over every source at once, as the harvest does; the ten index PDFs of 2015–2024 keep their own report
(`2026-09-12-acta-join-2015-2024.md`, regenerated). The *belief* beside an unmatched entry is the script's heuristic; the
reading in the prose is the author's.

### The reading

1. **The page column survives; what the OCR loses is a token here and there.** Unlike AAS 1 and 9-I (sample report §1),
   every volume of 1932–1957 renders its page column, and 22 of the 26 clear the spec's 95 % floor over the harvested
   categories (§4). The 4 below it -- 1936 (94.8 %), 1939 (94.1 %), 1948 (94.2 %), 1950 (93.5 %) -- lose their entries to
   the OCR of the text layer, not to a shape the parser lacks, and each is named in the fixture test with its cause: a
   page number misdrawn (`43G`, `III`, `1S8`, `5 M`, `2.18`, `i.62`, `31S`, `46T`, `c`), a page line dropped
   altogether (*Auspicia quaedam*, AAS 40), a line of dittos with no text, a year read `3918` (AAS 41) or `1961` (AAS 45,
   two years before the volume) that breaks the ditto chain of every letter after it until a year is printed, a month read
   `Die.` (AAS 42), and the lists a volume sets under one act with a page for each item (the Academy's members under the
   motu proprio *In multis solaciis*, AAS 28 (1936) 447–452; the ceremony of the Assumption under *Munificentissimus Deus*,
   AAS 42 (1950) 778–779; two radio messages of 1939 with neither a date column nor a dating formula). Each such line is
   listed under *Parser defects* below with the fixture's text, so a later pass can read the volume page for it.
2. **The OCR misdraws the date tokens far more often than 1931 or 1958 did, and every misreading the parser admits is
   measured.** The ditto mark comes as `»>`, `>>`, `))`, `.)`, `y>`, `«` or a lone letter (`» h 3`, `» D »`, `» s »`);
   punctuation sticks to a token (`.16`, `20\`, `.Martii`, `Nov,.`, `1950 Ian. • 14`); a token is doubled (`» Apr. Apr. 1`); a month
   is spelt `Man`, `Mah` (*Maii*: the constitution the first opens, AAS 25 (1933) 25, is dated *die secunda mensis Maii* at
   p. 28), `Marth`, `Innii`, `Apri`, `Ott`, `Noy`, `NOT`, `ÏTov`, `Doc`, each admitted only where a day follows; a year
   `i944`, `i 945`, `19.49`. `index.ts` names the volume each was measured on. A month it does not list is an unreadable
   date, reported, and the entries that inherit it by ditto are unreadable too until a month is printed -- never inherited
   from the entry before, which is what an unlisted word would silently have done. A year the index does not print -- a
   `»` in the year column with nothing above it (AAS 42 (1950) 911, the volume's first entries, *Munificentissimus Deus*
   and *Humani generis*), a token the OCR has broken (`19 IS`, `19Ö4`, `1ÍS50`, `3918`) or misread beyond repair
   (`1961` in a 1953 volume) -- dates the entry `????-MM-DD`, and the dittos after it inherit the blank until a year is
   printed (59 entries, §3): the volume year would be a guess (the seventeen letters after AAS 43's `1ÍS50 Ian. 29`,
   which the earlier parser dated 1949 by the entry above, are acts of 1950), so nothing is matched or minted from such an
   entry unless a curated row supplies the year from the act's own dating formula (`ACTA_INDEX_CORRECTIONS`: 23
   rows, each read in the volume PDF and agreeing with the index's month and day -- the head of AAS 42, *Ad Sinarum gentem*
   at the head of AAS 47, the constitutions and letters of 1948 under AAS 41's broken lines, the letters of 1951-1952 under
   AAS 45's). A year no volume can print but one digit from a year of the volume's span (`1047`, `1048`, `3950`, `3939`,
   `1963`, `1964`) is read as that year and *noted* on the entry and its dittos (26 entries, §3): the matcher may find
   the shelf record on the noted date, and the creator holds the entry as unresolvable rather than mint from a reading,
   unless a curated row confirms it against the act (*Singulari animi*, AAS 32 (1940) 42). A year the volume *could* print is
   never repaired, because the OCR's digits do not keep to one: AAS 41 (1949) prints `1919` for 1949 (*Conflictatio*
   *bonorum*), so each is corrected by a curated row quoting the act (three for AAS 41, one each for *Summi Pontificatus*
   (`1930`, AAS 31), *Ad catholici sacerdotii* (`Doc. 26` for 20 December, AAS 28) and *Vigilanti cura* (`1930 Iunii
   2$>`, AAS 28)), and the rest are held as dated before the pontificate (§9). A page check on one noted chain (AAS 45
   (1953): *Daniae (Hafniae)*, `1963` for 1953) found the index's page `587` to be the OCR's too -- the act opens at
   p. 537 -- which is why nothing is minted from a noted entry: the line that lost a digit in one column has lost it in
   another. *Auspicia quaedam* (AAS 40 (1948), 1 May 1948) stays uncited for another reason: the text layer drops the page line of
   its entry (`1048 Maii 1 Auspicia quaedam. …` runs into the next date), so no entry exists for a row to correct.
3. **The layout mode drifts a date onto the line before its entry, and sets blank-dated entries at a hanging indent.**
   Where the OCR's line boxes overlap, the layout mode prints an entry's date beside the last line of the entry before
   (AAS 27 (1935) 509: `» Apr. 4 rum stationalium evehuntur . 363` / `Paterna caritas. - Sancta Teresia …`); the parser
   gives such a date to the blank-dated entry that follows. And from 1939 the text of a dated entry can sit right after
   its date while a blank-dated entry keeps the page's hanging indent, one to eight columns short of the continuation
   lines (AAS 33 (1941) 533, *Tui in S. C. de Propaganda Fide*), so a line at that indent shaped as an entry opens
   (*Incipit. - Description*, *Toponym (vernacular). - …*) is one; on a page whose dated entries open that way, a
   capitalised continuation line at the entry column (`Sanctorum honores decernuntur 161`, AAS 47) is not.
4. **The columnar layout still dates some acts to the month, and the volumes list an act's translations under it.**
   120 entries print a month and no day (§1), kept with a month-precision date, matched by incipit within the month
   and never created (§9). Pius XII's radio messages and encyclicals are followed by their versions, each with a page
   (`Eius versiones a Statione radiophonica Civitatis Vaticanae editae: lingua gallica … 205`, AAS 33; `E textu latino
   versio anglica 645`, AAS 31): 36 such lines are consumed as sub-items of the act and left out of the
   parse rate's denominator, since they are the act again. Four encyclicals of Pius XI are indexed twice for the same
   reason -- the Latin text and, at its own page, the Spanish or Italian one (*Dilectissima Nobis* at AAS 25 (1933) 261
   and 275, *Mit brennender Sorge* at AAS 29 (1937) 145 and 168, *Divini Redemptoris* at 65 and 107, *Firmissimam*
   *constantiam* at 189 and 200) -- and the vernacular entries are held by curated rows quoting the pages (`ACTA_HOLDS`,
   §9), the Latin page being the citation (two by curated overrides, since the OCR misspells the Latin incipit).
5. **The index locator needed two more spellings.** The OCR reads the index heading's initial as `Í` (AAS 25, 1933; AAS
   32 (1940), whose *ÍNDICES NOMINUM* the locator missed, so that the first extraction ran 27 pages into the index of
   names) and once sets a full stop after it (AAS 46 (1954), `INDEX. DOCUMENTORUM`); the default extraction mode of
   AAS 25 drops the heading of the index's first page altogether, so `fetch-acta.sh` searches the layout mode when the
   default finds nothing. Every volume of the era has a chronological index.
6. **Every pope heading maps, in four OCR spellings.** `I. - ACTA PII PP. XI` and `I - ACTA PII PP. XII` are printed
   as `L - ACTA PII PP. XI` (1935, 1937), `1 - ACTA PII PP. XII` (1940), `I - ACTA Pii PP. XII` (1941) and `I - ACTA
   PII PP. Xll` (1949); the parser normalises the case and the numeral and records every heading as printed (§4). AAS
   31 (1939) carries `I - ACTA PII PP. XI` and `IV - ACTA PII PP. XII` with *Acta in morte Pii PP. XI* and *Acta
   Conclavis* between them, skipped as in 1958.

*Claimed twice* counts the documents two entries both match (§5), as the 2015–2024 report does; a document claimed from
two sources counts in each. *Unmatched* counts the entries of a harvested or partly harvested category the join left without a document (each is
listed in §6 with a belief); *Created* and *Held* partition them, with the ambiguous and doubly-claimed entries, by the
creator's rules (§8, §9). *Dated > 1 year before the volume* counts the acts a volume publishes late (spec §2: an entry can be
dated years earlier; 1917 prints letters of 1910 and 1915). *Documents of the popes without an entry* counts the harvested
shelf documents of the source's popes dated in the volume year that carry no `acta` (§11).

### The reading

1. **144 references written, every one from a quoted index line (§12):** 2 curated, 3 incipit, 1 toponym, 138 unique. The shelves of Pius XI
   and Pius XII are thin -- 18 and 227 of their shelf records are dated in the era, against the 2214 entries the twenty-six
   volumes print in harvested categories -- so most of what the index names is unmatched, and the *unique* rule carries the join; the *toponym* and
   *incipit* matches include the claims the evidence rule resolved (`match.ts`), two the curated overrides settle (the
   Latin texts of *Dilectissima Nobis* and *Firmissimam constantiam*, §4), and the acts whose year the index does not print
   and a curated row supplies -- among them the registry's dogmatic-definition bull *Munificentissimus Deus* and *Humani generis*
   at the head of AAS 42, and *Ad Sinarum gentem* at the head of AAS 47 (§1.2).
2. **1627 documents created** (§8) -- `rp:pius-xi` 468, `rp:pius-xii` 1159 -- and 443 entries held (§9), 33 of them by the
   duplicate guard and 4 by the id-collision rule, 59 by the OCR rule, 10 by the page rule. 304 constitutions print toponym and incipit both; the constitutions of
   1932–1945 print the see, with its vernacular in parentheses, and no incipit (*De Sienhsien (De Kinghsien). - Vicariatus*
   *Apostolicus …*), and the letters of the 1930s for a minor basilica are entered under the diocese (*Passaviensis dioecesis. -*),
   which the parser reads as toponyms, so they mint provisionally with the see in the title (§8). The *Epistulae* are
   created for both popes, whose letters shelves are harvested. An incipit the OCR has damaged -- a mark or digit no
   incipit carries, a full stop inside it, a lower-case initial (*ut Pater*, which drops the sample's 1978 count by one) --
   is held rather than minted into an id the page does not print (§9, *OCR-damaged*).
3. **The volumes print two short letters on one page as a matter of course, and the OCR misdraws a page number onto
   another act's.** Four pages of the era open two acts each -- AAS 24 (1932) 39, AAS 26 (1934) 19, AAS 28 (1936) 102, AAS 45
   (1953) 91 -- each read in the volume and curated in `ACTA_SHARED_PAGES` with the page quoted, so invariant 25 admits
   exactly those pairs. 10 other entries cite a page another entry or a matched document cites, where the volume
   prints one act (AAS 42 (1950) 37 and 42 for 373, 375, 421 and 423; AAS 43 (1951) 660 for 666; AAS 46 (1954) 753 for 756;
   AAS 49 (1957) 825 for 823) or lists one act twice (AAS 45 (1953) 782, *Simulacrum*): the creator holds them by a new
   rule, *page-shared* (`create.ts`), for a curated page correction this phase does not attempt.
4. **Documents of the era's popes dated in the volume years without a reference** (§11): the shelves' own December acts
   (the next volume's), the acts whose index line the OCR damaged (§3), the constitutions of one day the join could not
   tell apart (§5), and the classes the index files under a category the registry does not attempt.

Decisions taken here with the evidence beside each row of `categories.ts` (the sample's decisions stand): *Epistulae*
*encyclicae* (1937, 1948, 1950: *Mit brennender Sorge*, *In multiplicibus curis*, *Anni sacri* …) and the singular *Epistula*
*encyclica* (1933–1954) map to the encyclicals row, every act among them being on its pope's encyclicals shelf; *Bulla*
*dogmatica* (1950, *Munificentissimus Deus*) to the constitutions row, since vatican.va's apost_constitutions shelf carries
it; the OCR spellings *Litteeae* / *Littebae Apostolicae*, *Littebae* / *Litterae Decketales*, *Motti proprio*, *Bpisttjlae*,
*Epistulas*, *Aliocutiones*, *Sacka Consistoria*, *Iustructio pastoralis* and the singulars *Chirographus*, *Sacrum*
*Consistorium*, *Nuntius scripto datus*, *Nuntius telegraphicus*, *Sollemnis conventio* to their rows; *Adhortatio*
*radiophonica* (1952, to the faithful of Rome) to *Nuntii radiophonici*, counted for #27. Two headings cover two classes
of act at once and become `partly` rows the creator never creates from: the bare *Adhortatio*, which is the 2019 joint
appeal on Jerusalem in one index and Pius XII's exhortation *I rapidi progressi* (1 January 1954, on the apost_exhortations
shelf) in another, and *Hortatio* / *Hortatio pastoralis* / *Hortationes* / *Iustructio pastoralis*, Pius XII's Lenten
addresses to the parish priests of Rome and his appeal of 31 August 1939 to the governments (*Le Souverain Pontife*)
beside one apostolic exhortation (*In auspicando super*, 28 June 1948, on the shelf): the matcher writes the reference the
shelf evidences and the creator holds the rest (`NOT_CREATED`). New rows with no registry class: *Sollemnes*
*canonizationes* (the canonisation ceremonies of 1938–1954, a proclamation and a homily per entry, each with a page) and
*Orationes* (the prayers of 1942–1953). No heading is left `unknown`.

### Pages two matched acts cite, withheld

None: every page two matched documents of the era cite is curated in `ACTA_SHARED_PAGES` with the volume page quoted, and
invariant 25 admits exactly those pairs (4 pages of the era).

### Acts the Acta print twice

None among the era's sources.

### Matches a curated reference displaces

A row of `ACTA_CURATED_REFERENCES` (curation.ts) that names the match it supersedes, with the evidence that the matched entry is
not the act's citation of record (controller ruling 15): the match is neither a claim nor a record, and the document cites the row's page.
None among the era's sources.

### Pages the index prints wrongly, corrected

A row of `ACTA_PAGE_CORRECTIONS` (curation.ts) replaces the page an index line prints -- the OCR's digit, or the index's own slip --
with the page the volume opens the act at, both read; the entry is matched, created and checked for a shared page at the act's page.
None among the era's sources.

## 8. Created from the Acta

The data carries **1627** AAS-only records from the era and the creator, re-run here over the shelf records, produces **1627** — the same set, entry for entry, and the same records field for field (ids aside, which the collision and ordinal passes assign).

Each record carries `source.url` = the whole-volume PDF for a volume source and `null` for an index PDF (spec 2a §4), the
fixture's `retrieved` date, `source.shelf` `aas/{year}`, and `acta.part` for a double volume (`"I"` for 1917).

By class: apostolic-exhortation 1; apostolic-letter+motu-proprio 21; apostolic-letter 541; letter 436; papal-bull+apostolic-constitution 592; papal-bull 36. Provisional (no incipit read): 322.

**Circumscription material.** Of the 592 AAS-born constitutions of the era, the index describes 441 with an erection or elevation
verb (*conditur*, *erigitur*, *constituitur*, *dismembrato*, *evehitur*, *attollitur*, *extollitur*); none carries `keywords` or `actKind` (spec 2a §4).

### Shelf ids re-minted by densification

**None.** No AAS-only provisional record shares an ordinal group (issuer, genre, date) with a shelf provisional record, and
the shelf's ordinals are what a pass over the shelf records alone assigns; no minted shelf id gained a full-date suffix.

The era prints 169 radio messages under *Nuntii radiophonici* and its variants -- Pius XII's from the first of his pontificate
(*Con inmenso gozo*, 1939-04-16, AAS 31 (1939) 151) through the Christmas messages of the war years, with their versions listed beneath -- and Pius XI's of 1934 and 1938;
3 matched harvested *Urbi et Orbi* records (`mag:pius-xii/urbi-et-orbi-easter-1952`, `mag:pius-xii/urbi-et-orbi-easter-1954`, `mag:pius-xii/urbi-et-orbi-easter-1957`). That is the
count #27 asks for (`medium: radio`), recorded here and applied nowhere: no AAS-born record carries `medium`.
